sections.heading: You Wanted a Second Opinion, Not a Sales Pitch
body: A shingle lifts in the wind, or a brown ring spreads across the ceiling, and every roofer you call seems to have the same answer: replace it. You can't climb up and check for yourself, so you end up trusting whoever sounds the most sure.

That's a lot to hand a stranger. A roof is one of the biggest bills on a house, and it's hard to judge from the ground. Before any quote, you need someone who will look and tell you what's really going on.

sections.heading: We Tell You What the Roof Needs, and What It Doesn't
body: We start by looking at the roof and explaining what we see in plain words. Then we lay out your choices. If it's a small repair, we say so. If the roof is worn out, we say that too, and give you a detailed estimate.
Dusty Rieck owns Sandhill Roofing, and his name comes up in review after review.

Your choices laid out before you decide anything

sections.heading: Finally, a Straight Answer From Someone Who Knows Roofs
body: A roof call usually starts with a question you can't answer on your own: what do I have, and what does it need? Here's how it feels when somebody finally answers it.

sections.quote: As a new home owner I called 15 different roofing companies and 7 different shingle suppliers to figure out what type of roof I had. Dusty answered my call and immediately gave me proper guidance, knowledge, and went over the top to help me figure out my issue.
sections.name: Joe B.

sections.heading: What You're Seeing Up There, and What It Usually Means
body: Something you can see from the yard or from inside the house is usually what starts the call. Here's what it often points to.

items.title: Shingles missing or lifted after a windy day
items.text: Wind can break a shingle's seal and lift it, and the next gust takes more. Sometimes that's a repair, and we'll say so when it is.

items.title: A stain or drip on the ceiling
items.text: Water can run along the framing before it shows inside, so the stain isn't always under the opening. Sometimes the cause isn't the roof at all.

items.title: Granules in the gutters, or shingles curling and cracking
items.text: That usually means the roof is wearing out across a whole slope, not in one spot. A patch buys a little time, so price a replacement beside it.

items.title: Dents or bruises after hail
items.text: Hail damage is easy to miss from the ground. A look on the roof is the only way to know what it did.

tail: Not sure which one you've got? Call (402) 890-6460 and describe what you see.

sections.quote: Dusty came out and looked at a leak in our ceiling that we assumed was due to a roof issue. … Although the issue wasn't with the roof, he knew exactly where it was and who we should contact …
sections.name: Darion M.

sections.heading: Years Later, You Can Still Call the Company That Did Your Roof

sections.quote: I contacted Dusty to ask for documentation about a roof that he installed nine years ago. … He promptly and cheerfully provided the info. Our customers were happy with the roof Dusty installed and were very pleased that he continues to provide excellent service years later!

body: After hail or wind, the roof is only half of it. The other half is the claim. Insurance claims are part of the work we handle, and we walk you through what's needed from the roof side.
We can't tell you what your insurer will decide, and your agent is the one to ask about your policy and your deductible. What we can do is show you what's on the roof and help with the paperwork.

sections.heading: Is It Time for a New Roof, or Is It a Repair?
body: Walk the yard and look up. Cracked or curling shingles, bare spots and granules washing into the gutters usually mean the whole roof is wearing out, not just one spot.
A patch on a roof like that buys a little time. If the whole slope is going, the money is better spent on the roof itself.

The opposite is just as true. A lifted shingle or a loose flashing is a repair, and replacing a roof that's mostly sound costs you money for nothing. Telling you which one you have is the first thing we do.
list: Cracked, curling or missing shingles in more than one area
A leak that comes back after a patch
Hail or wind damage across the roof

sections.heading: What a Good Estimate Spells Out
body: Whichever roofer you call, ask what the estimate covers. A replacement price depends on a handful of things, and a number with no detail behind it is hard to compare.

items.title: Size and pitch
items.text: More roof means more material and labor, and a steeper roof takes longer to work on safely.

items.title: Material
items.text: Shingles, steel and slate-look roofs sit at very different prices. The estimate should name the one you're getting.

items.title: What comes off first
items.text: Layers of old roofing add labor. So does any wood underneath that has to be replaced once the old roof is gone.

items.title: The details
items.text: Chimneys, vents, valleys and flashing each add work, and they're where leaks tend to start. A good estimate doesn't skip them.

items.title: Cleanup
items.text: Tear-off throws shingles and nails across the yard, so ask how the crew handles it.

tail: Our estimate for a roof replacement is free, and you see your choices and the numbers before you decide anything.

sections.quote: Dusty provided a detailed estimate with a few choices and then his crew executed the plan as described. … There was a slight oversight area but Dusty was out not the next day but the next morning and made it right. Quality and Craftsmanship still exists!
sections.name: Tim L.

sections.heading: Choosing the Material
body: We install asphalt shingles, steel, stone coated steel, standing seam steel, rubber slate, polymer and cedar shake roofs, plus shingles built to resist impact. Each one fits a different house and budget.

**Asphalt shingles** cost the least up front and come in plenty of colors. **Steel** and **standing seam steel** cost more and are made to last longer. **Stone coated steel** is a metal roof with a stone-granule surface.

**Rubber slate** and **polymer** roofs go for the look of slate or shake without the weight. **Cedar shake** is the classic natural look and takes more care. **Impact-resistant shingles** are worth asking about, since hail is hard on every roof.
Tell us what matters most, whether that's price, how long it lasts, how it looks or how it handles hail, and we'll say which one fits.

sections.quote: I love my new steel roof! Whatever kind of roof you want, call Sandhill Roofing. Mr. Dusty did a great job explaining options (many!) and making sure I got what I wanted.

sections.heading: When a Storm Is Why You Need a New Roof
body: Hail and wind are the usual reasons a roof has to come off. If there's an insurance claim, we handle that side of it with you and explain what we find on the roof.
We can't promise what your insurance company will decide, and your agent is the one to ask about your policy and deductible. Take dated photos of the damage if you can.

sections.heading: How a Replacement Goes, Start to Finish
body: On any roof replacement, the order is the same. The old roof comes off, the wood underneath gets checked, and the new roof goes on, with flashing and vents around it. Then the yard gets cleaned up.
Start to finish, it usually comes down to your decisions on the material and the date. Once we've seen the roof, you'll know what to expect.

sections.heading: What Lincoln Homeowners Ask About a New Roof

items.q: How much does a roof replacement cost?
items.a: It depends on the size and pitch of the roof, the material, how many layers come off and what the wood underneath needs. A number given without seeing the roof is a guess, so the free estimate is where you get the real figure.

items.q: How do I know whether I need a replacement or a repair?
items.a: Look for damage across the whole roof, not one spot: curling or cracked shingles, bare patches, granules in the gutters. If you're not sure, call and describe what you see.

items.q: Will insurance pay for a new roof?
items.a: That depends on your policy, your deductible and what caused the damage. Your agent can answer it, and we can show you what's on the roof.

items.q: How long does a roof replacement take?
items.a: The size and pitch of your roof, the material and the weather all play a part. After we've looked at the roof, we'll give you an idea of the timing.

items.q: Will I get a sales pitch with the estimate?
items.a: Call (402) 890-6460, say what the roof is doing, and ask for the free estimate. The first thing you'll hear is whether you need a new roof at all.

footer.about: Sandhill Roofing is a family-owned roofing company based in Lincoln, serving Eastern Nebraska. We handle roofing, siding, gutters, windows and doors, and insurance claims.
why: A straight answer on your roof

Your customers already make your case. 101 people have reviewed Sandhill Roofing on Google, and one thing keeps coming up: Dusty tells you what the roof needs and what it doesn't. mike B. wrote that he "didn't make me feel pressured or try to sell me on things that I didn't need."

Your website shows none of it. It's one homepage of about 362 words with no headline Google can read, no reviews, and a services page whose headings are your phone number, five times over. Nothing on it says roofer, or Lincoln.
So we built a site that opens with roofer in Lincoln, NE, leads with the straight answer your customers describe, and gives roof replacement a page of its own.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your site shows no street address, while your Google listing puts you at 8120 Trendwood Dr, Lincoln, NE 68506, so which address should every listing use?
Your site headlines a lifetime workmanship warranty on roofing, siding and gutters but doesn't say what it covers, so what are the terms we should show?
Your site says you serve Eastern Nebraska without naming a town, while your reviews mention a property in Henderson and a home much closer to Omaha, so which towns should every listing name?

lead.heading: Why we led with the straight answer
lead.text: The scariest moment for a Lincoln homeowner is a roofer's quote for a whole new roof, and not knowing whether it's true. Your reviews are full of customers describing the opposite, a straight answer on what the roof needs and what it doesn't, and none of the competitor sites we could read says anything like it. That gives Google and AI tools something no generic roofing page has: your real reviews and your way of working.
